name: SS Yongala

sources.title: SS Yongala — Armstrong Whitworth 1903: length 106.7 m, beam 13.8 m, depth 8.3 m, single screw; the wreck on her starboard side listing 60-70°, bow on 347°, seabed about 30 m, upper parts at 16 m; superstructure intact, ventilators and railings collapsed, sand scoured from the starboard side
Yongala Dive — history of the wreck: on her starboard side, 14 m on top, 28 m on the sand, 109 m long, coral encrusted
Yongala Dive — marine life on the wreck (Queensland groper at the bow, giant trevally, Maori wrasse, rays, turtles, sea snakes)

notes: Built by code (model_sources/Q1424289_yongala.py, tools/meshkit.py, tools/dresskit.py) with AI assistance. The hull whole, on her starboard side at 65° (published: 60-70°), bow on 347°; the saloon and boat-deck houses, bridge and davits still in place, the hatches open with general cargo (crates, casks, bales); the ventilators and railings collapsed onto the sand with some crates; single propeller and rudder. The funnel and the masts are not described in the sources: here they have fallen and lie on the sand. She is a protected site and the grave of 122 people. Colours and the exact layout of the superstructure are approximate. model_built.glb: the ship as she sailed (1903-1911). No marine life in the model: Offlined draws the living things itself.
